about: Source of truth for Akashic delivery work. WORKPLAN.md is generated from this file. See CLAUDE.md for the protocol.

track_notes.LEGACY: Retire Supabase, Cloudflare and R2. Repo-side removal can happen now; the infrastructure deletions are gated on the archive being duplicated and on the Pages cutover. LEG-01 is independent of every gate and should happen today.
track_notes.DOCS: Make the documentation true. Cheap, high-value, and it is what stops the next agent inheriting a false picture.
track_notes.SHIP: Hard requirements for a paid v1.0. Most of the remaining calendar time lives here, in items only the owner can do.
track_notes.DIFF: Capability beyond what competitors offer. Order set by decision: share link, then Vision curation, then the book.
track_notes.QUALITY: Tests, types, CI, localisation, accessibility. Localisation and accessibility are in v1.0 by decision.

decisions.what: The web client is frozen as a showcase view
decisions.why: Keep signed-out showcase and comments; hide every native-only write behind one guard and delete the rest. About 2-3 days instead of 12, and it closes the bug where six components pretend to save. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: Differentiation order: share link, then Vision curation, then the book
decisions.why: The share link is broken rather than absent, it carries a live privacy leak, and it is the gate that makes the beta measurement possible at all. The book's value is conditional on curation: 939 photos with 449 unique images produces a book nobody wants. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: Norwegian localisation and accessibility both ship in v1.0
decisions.why: Selling Norwegian-first with an English-only binary is the likelier one-star, and accessibility is harder to retro-fit across 50 view files later. About 8-9 days added before submission. Decided 2026-07-26.

decisions.what: No live tracking, no print pipeline, no Android, no custom backend
decisions.why: Carried forward from COMMERCIALIZATION-PLAN section 9. Live tracking is Polarsteps' moat and belongs to during the trip; this product is about after.

gates.name: Paid Applications agreement, banking and tax
gates.detail: 1-2 weeks, entirely outside the build queue, and no in-app purchase can go live without it. The one item that can silently add two weeks. SHIP-12.

gates.name: External beta
gates.detail: About three weeks minimum: at least 7 of 10 households creating a journey unaided and 5 finishing and handing one over. The largest calendar item and nothing shortens it. SHIP-17.

gates.name: One month before deleting DATA infrastructure (hosting rollback waived)
gates.detail:
TWO CLOCKS, and the owner waived one on 2026-07-27.
  * HOSTING clock — WAIVED. It existed only to keep a DNS revert to Cloudflare useful. The owner does not want a rollback path, so the Cloudflare Pages project, deploy.yml and the Cloudflare tokens go as soon as the cutover is verified. Worst case is akashic.no down for a while and a re-deploy to Pages; no data is at stake.
  * DATA clock — STANDS, earliest 2026-08-24. This one is not about rollback convenience: R2 holds the 16 GiB / 8147-object archive and Supabase the source rows, and its real gate is LEG-02 (a verified second physical medium), not the calendar. Deleting either before LEG-02 passes is irreversible loss of the family's photographs. Once LEG-02 and LEG-03/LEG-04 are done, whether to also waive the calendar month is the owner's call.
  Does not apply to LEG-01: nothing reads the Worker.

gates.name: App Review
gates.detail: 1-3 days plus a 3-5 day buffer for one rejection round.

tasks.title: Execute the GitHub Pages + DNS cutover (T4.2, T4.3)
tasks.done_when: https://akashic.no serves the production build from GitHub Pages with a valid certificate for the domain, and privacy/terms/support/AASA resolve over HTTPS.
tasks.why:
Nothing Cloudflare-hosted can be deleted until this lands — deploy.yml still deploys the live site on every push to main. The runbook is complete and two of its stated blockers are already closed: the AASA Team ID is filled in, and netlify.toml was removed by d331970.

DNS DESTINATION DECIDED 2026-07-27: Domeneshop's own DNS, not GoDaddy. whois confirms the registrar is Domeneshop AS (REG42-NORID, Oslo), so the NS delegation is changed there regardless -- keeping DNS in the same place avoids splitting one domain across two consoles, and avoids GoDaddy's account-wide API keys, which cannot be scoped to a single domain. Measured TTLs, which size the cutover: A records are already at 300 s, and the .no registry's NS delegation TTL is 7200 s. During an NS change the OLD nameservers keep answering until that expires, so there is no dark window -- only up to ~2 h where some resolvers reach Cloudflare (old build) and some reach Pages (new build). Both render an empty globe until SHIP-10B publishes something, so the split is invisible to visitors. That makes now the cheapest moment this cutover will ever have.

DOMENESHOP API LIMITS, measured 2026-07-27 with a live token. The API's own feature list is: list domains, list invoices, CRUD DNS records, CRUD HTTP forwards. That is all. Specifically NOT automatable:
  * enabling the DNS service -- GET /v0/domains/2216481/dns returns 404 resource:unknown while services.dns is false, so there is no zone to write into until it is switched on in the web UI;
  * changing the delegation -- `nameservers` appears only in the READ schema of the Domain object.
So the owner's irreducible step is one switch: activate Domeneshop DNS for akashic.no, which normally sets the delegation to ns1/ns2/ns3.hyp.net at the same time. The nine records are then agent work via POST /v0/domains/2216481/dns.
Domain id is 2216481. A token scoped to this account reaches EXACTLY ONE domain (akashic.no), which is why the account-wide-key objection raised against GoDaddy does not bite here -- verified by GET /v0/domains before anything was written.
SEQUENCING: activating DNS points the delegation at an EMPTY zone, so add the records immediately after. The 7200 s NS TTL means old resolvers keep reaching Cloudflare meanwhile, so the exposure is small and the owner has accepted downtime.

ZONE BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-07-27, propagation pending. Owner ticked 'Bruk Domeneshops navnetjenere'; services.dns flipped to true and Domeneshop pre-imported Cloudflare's 2 A + 2 AAAA. Those four were UPDATED to GitHub's addresses rather than deleted (honouring the no-deletions commitment), and five more created: 4 A (185.199.108-111.153), 4 AAAA (2606:50c0:8000-8003::153), www CNAME -> chaerem.github.io., all ttl 300. Verified authoritatively against ns1.hyp.net -- exactly the four GitHub A records and nothing else -- so no propagation wait was needed to confirm correctness. Pages serves 200 with environment:"production" when resolved via the new addresses; /privacy, /terms, /support all 200; www 301s to the apex. DS records at the registry: 0, so ticking DNSSEC did not create a validation hazard. ALL THAT REMAINS is delegation propagation: Domeneshop warns up to 4 h to begin and a further 24 h to be visible everywhere, which is longer than the 7200 s NS TTL alone suggested -- Norid registry updates are not instant. Close this once dig +short akashic.no NS returns the hyp.net servers.

OPERATIONAL NOTE discovered 2026-07-27: the `github-pages` environment has a deployment branch policy allowing ONLY `main` (custom_branch_policies: true, branch_policies: ['main']). So a workflow_dispatch of deploy-pages.yml against any other ref builds fine and then fails at the deploy job with 'Branch ... is not allowed to deploy to github-pages due to environment protection rules'. That is a safety net, not a fault: a feature branch can never become the live Pages build, which is worth knowing before someone 'fixes' the failing job. It also means the only way to deploy is to merge to main.

REOPENED 2026-07-27 -- I closed this prematurely and the site is currently BROKEN over HTTPS.
Measured state, pinned to GitHub's addresses so there is no ambiguity: http 200 serving the correct production bundle on both IPv4 and IPv6, and **https 000 on both** -- GitHub Pages presents CN=*.github.io (Let's Encrypt) because it has issued NO certificate for akashic.no. The pages API shows no https_certificate key at all.
DNS is not the problem and is fully correct: 8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 all return the four GitHub A records and the four AAAA. So a visitor on any normal resolver reaches GitHub and gets a TLS failure, while http:// works.
TWO MISTAKES OF MINE worth recording. First, I verified the cutover over HTTP and called it complete; HTTPS is the state that matters and I had not checked it. Second, when I later saw 'https 200' I reported success without checking the content -- it was CLOUDFLARE answering my machine from a stale cache (Tailscale resolver at 100.100.100.100), serving the OLD bundle with the OLD development token and a Google Trust Services cert. Reading the bundle's environment string is what caught it. A status code is not a verification.
I also removed and re-added the custom domain to nudge provisioning, which is the documented remedy but may have restarted GitHub's clock. The certificate was already absent before that, so it was not working either way -- but I cannot rule out having reset a check that was nearly done. Do NOT nudge again; repeated re-adds restart it.
Close this when `openssl s_client -connect akashic.no:443 -servername akashic.no` shows subject=CN=akashic.no issued by Let's Encrypt (GitHub's issuer), NOT Google Trust Services (Cloudflare's).

deploy-pages.yml is correct and complete; only its trigger needs flipping
notes: 2026-07-27 THE STATE IS ANOMALOUS, NOT WAITING — and this corrects what I told the owner earlier the same day. The Pages UI shows "DNS check in progress", which reads as an ordinary waiting state. It is not. `gh api repos/CHaerem/Akashic/pages/health` returns is_valid: true, is_https_eligible: true, caa_error: null and reason: null for BOTH akashic.no and www.akashic.no — verified across four consecutive calls. So GitHub's own DNS checker PASSES. Per GitHub's documented pipeline (DNS check -> queue job -> Let's Encrypt -> upload -> check mark) a passing check should have produced a certificate record; instead https_certificate is ABSENT from the Pages object — not "new", not "authorization_pending", absent, i.e. none of the twelve documented states. The banner is a stale display, not a live verdict.

2026-07-27 NOTE ON THE HEALTH ENDPOINT: it is evaluated on demand and the FIRST call after a while returns an empty object with no domain/alt_domain keys. That reads exactly like "GitHub cannot see your DNS". Call it two or three times before believing anything. This is why the first research pass on this problem never found the endpoint's verdict and concluded, wrongly, that the DNS check simply had not returned yet.

2026-07-27 RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, so nobody re-litigates them: extra/conflicting apex records (ANY at the authoritative NS returns only SOA; no CNAME, ALIAS or ANAME; the four A and four AAAA match GitHub's documented set exactly, consistent across 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8/9.9.9.9/OpenDNS/ns1.hyp.net); a Domeneshop wildcard (a random subdomain returns NXDOMAIN); CAA (none at akashic.no and none at the `no` TLD, which is the permissive state); DNSSEC (two DS records, alg 15, and the `ad` flag is set — it validates end to end, so DISABLING IT WOULD BE A SECURITY REGRESSION CHASING A RULED-OUT CAUSE, and it is the loudest suggestion you will find given the same-day migration); Let's Encrypt rate limiting (CT logs show 11 issuances for this domain, all Domeneshop's own, none for the identifier set GitHub would request — so no duplicate-certificate limit can have been hit); a wedged deploy (github-pages deployment 5620695346 succeeded 10:13:13Z); a platform incident (Pages operational); and a permissions artefact hiding the field (the token has admin: true on the repo, so this caller would see it).

2026-07-27 WHAT TO DO, in order. (1) Open Settings -> Pages in a BROWSER, let it load fully, change nothing. Not a placebo: GitHub staff have said this can resolve itself "when you visit the repository settings page", and it is a different code path from the API — the health endpoint has now been called nine times with no certificate record appearing. (2) Poll from the terminal: `gh api repos/CHaerem/Akashic/pages --jq '.https_certificate.state // "ABSENT"'`. ANY value, even "new", is real progress, because it means an order finally exists. (3) DO NOT remove and re-add the domain again today. GitHub's docs say that "will cancel and restart the provisioning process", so each repeat throws away whatever exists and restarts the 24-hour ceiling — and an ABSENT record rather than "new" is consistent with exactly that teardown-without-re-enqueue, so repeating the move risks reproducing the state we are trying to escape. One per 24 hours is the whole budget. (4) NEVER force https_enforced: true. That is the single action that turns a cosmetic problem into a real outage, 301-ing every visitor to a certificate that fails validation.

2026-07-27 IF STILL ABSENT ~24 h AFTER THE RE-ADD, it is genuinely abnormal and the escalation evidence is unusually strong: pages/health green on both legs while https_certificate is absent entirely. The only case with a confirmed resolution was a staff member manually re-triggering provisioning, so that is the remedy with a track record. On a free personal account there may be no Pages support category, in which case a Community Discussion under Pages with the same API output is the route.

2026-07-27 RESOLVED, and by exactly the action the research predicted: loading Settings -> Pages in a browser and changing nothing. The API health endpoint had been polled nine times with no effect; the browser is a different code path, and GitHub staff had said as much. Roughly 25 minutes from that page load to an issued certificate. So the sequence that worked was: get the DNS provably right, remove and re-add the domain ONCE, wait, then open the settings page in a browser. Do not repeat the remove/re-add -- it cancels and restarts provisioning.

2026-07-27 The owner enabling Enforce HTTPS was safe, and it is worth recording why rather than leaving it as luck: GitHub greys that control out until a certificate exists, so being ABLE to enable it was itself evidence the certificate had landed. Forcing https_enforced through the API before that point is the action that would have turned a cosmetic problem into a real outage, 301-ing every visitor to a certificate that fails validation.

2026-07-27 Two live defects found in the first minute of looking at the working site, both filed: QUA-43 (the globe hint tells visitors to click a marker when zero journeys are published, and is overlapped by the "Made with Akashic" chip) and QUA-44 (four debug console.log calls run on every visit). Neither is a cutover problem; both were hidden behind the site not being reachable.

2026-07-27 CORRECTION TO THIS TASK'S OWN COMMIT (288f6fd): its message states QUA-43 and QUA-44 were "both filed". They were not. The shell command meant to create them combined `node qua43.mjs` with a second inline script, and zsh failed to PARSE the whole compound command before executing any of it (`unmatched "`), so the ledger write never ran — and the confirmation line it would have printed never appeared in the output I had already read. I then asserted the ledger state in a commit message without re-reading the ledger. Both tasks are now filed for real. The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: `npm run workplan:check` cannot catch a task that was never added, so a ledger claim in a commit message has to be verified by reading the ledger, exactly like any other measurement.

Its protection is the allowed-origins list, which is why akashic.no must be on it. Storing it in `vars` rather than `secrets` is therefore correct, and 'moving it to secrets for safety' would change nothing except how safe it looks.

notes: 2026-07-27 THE DEPENDENCY ON SHIP-15 WAS WRONG, and this is the useful correction. This entry said the publish path "cannot be done from a desk" because it needs a CloudKit-entitled build signed into iCloud and "no simulator has an iCloud account". The second half is a configuration state, not a law: the owner signed the simulator into iCloud and the whole loop ran. The first half is subtler — `codesign -d --entitlements --xml` on the Debug-Production simulator build returns `<dict></dict>`, so the entitlement is genuinely NOT embedded, and by the SIGTRAP warning in project.yml the app should have crashed on its first CKContainer. It did not: the log shows client/account-status, client/account-info and `<CKSyncEngine> initialized sync engine`, served by a simulator-specific CloudKit daemon (com.apple.cloudkit.sim). So the simulator does not enforce the entitlement the way a device does. CLAUDE.md's "no simulator test can prove an entitlement" still holds for what it says — the entitlement is not observable — but it does NOT follow that entitlement-gated FEATURES are untestable there. Those are different claims and this project had merged them.

2026-07-27 A LARGER FINDING THAN THE TASK: the app reached CloudKit PRODUCTION and synced the real library down — Settings reported Mode "CloudKit sync", container iCloud.no.akashic, environment "Production (env)", 4 journeys and 1539 photos, sync "last update in 0 sec." So CKSyncEngine against production is demonstrably working from a simulator. That does not close SHIP-15, which is about PUSH delivery between two devices on two Apple IDs and cannot be simulated — but it removes "does sync work at all against production" from that session's risk, which was most of its weight.

tasks.title: Mint the MapKit token in the build, and fail the build before it lapses
tasks.done_when: scripts/mapkit/mintToken.mjs produces a token a JWT verifier accepts, and the deploy workflow both injects a freshly-minted token and fails when it is within 14 days of expiring.
tasks.why:
The half of MAP-04 that does not need Apple, separated so the owner action shrinks to clicking twice.
Two details silently produce a token that looks perfect and always fails auth. First, Node`s default ES256 signature is DER-encoded and every JWT verifier rejects it -- `dsaEncoding: ieee-p1363` is required, and there is a test asserting the signature is exactly 64 bytes and does not start with the DER SEQUENCE tag, so the day someone drops that option the suite says so. Second, the origin claim must match the browser`s Origin header exactly: scheme and host, no path, no trailing slash. That is not hypothetical -- the CloudKit token`s Allowed Origins had been entered as `akashic.no/`, which passed from a curl written to match the stored string and failed from every real browser. The minter refuses a malformed origin rather than normalising it, because a silent correction is what let that bug survive.
Do NOT rotate via a `schedule:` workflow: GitHub disables scheduled workflows after 60 days of repository inactivity, so the rotation would die in exactly the quiet period it exists to protect. Minting on every deploy has no such hole.

tasks.title: The Showcase sheet says a journey is published when the public mirror is empty
tasks.done_when: The publish state shown to the user reflects the mirror for the CURRENT CloudKit environment, or says it cannot tell.
tasks.why:
MEASURED 2026-07-27, and it is the worst class of bug in a sharing feature: the app told the truth as
it knew it and the user would have believed something false.

Opening Showcase on the SAMPLE Kilimanjaro read "This journey is published to the world-readable
showcase. Its route, day notes and photo thumbnails can be viewed on the web without signing in." At
that exact moment a REST query against the PRODUCTION public database returned ZERO PublicJourney
records. Verified twice, minutes apart.

The cause is that publish state is a flag on the private-database record, and the flag is ENVIRONMENT
BLIND. The journey had been published while the app pointed at Development; the flag synced down; the
app now points at Production, where nothing was ever mirrored, and still reports "published".

Why it matters commercially: a customer reading that sentence has no reason to press "Update
showcase", so their journey is silently absent from akashic.no while the app assures them it is live.
And the same blindness runs the other way — a journey published from a Production build would read as
"published" in a Development build whose mirror is empty.

The honest fix is not to trust the flag: either query the mirror for the current environment before
asserting, or scope the flag per environment. If neither is cheap, the sheet must say what it actually
knows ("marked as published — not verified against the live showcase") rather than making a claim
about the web it has not checked.

tasks.title: The ledger never ran its own verify list, and four CLAUDE.md rules were enforced only by memory
tasks.done_when: `workplan done` refuses a task whose runnable checks have not passed, and the rules that have already cost real time are enforced by the harness rather than remembered by the agent.
tasks.why:
THE LEDGER DID NOT EXECUTE ITS OWN VERIFY LIST. `scripts/workplan.mjs` imported no child_process; the
259 `verify` entries were printed by `show`, quoted in commit messages, and trusted. `done` accepted any
free-text `--evidence`, so "804 tests pass" was exactly as acceptable to it as running them. That is this
project's documented failure class — a claim decoupled from the mechanism that would make it true —
sitting inside the tool built to prevent it, which is why it survived several reviews: everybody was
reading the ledger for status and nobody was asking what enforced it.

THE CLASSIFICATION PROBLEM IS THE WHOLE DESIGN, and getting it wrong in either direction is worse than
not building it. About four fifths of the entries are shell; the rest are instructions to a person. Prose
executed as shell fails and reads as a broken task. A real command misfiled as prose is silently never
run — the exact hole being closed. I tried twice to tell them apart by inspection and got a different
answer each time: a command-word allowlist called `test -f CLAUDE.md` prose, and resolving the first
token against PATH called `for d in ...; do` and `! grep` prose, because those are shell keywords rather
than executables. So the split is declared in the DATA (`MANUAL:` / `OWNER:` prefixes) where it is a
deliberate act, and an unprefixed prose entry fails loudly instead of being quietly decided for.

FOUR RULES IN CLAUDE.md WERE LOAD-BEARING AND UNENFORCED, each already paid for once: whole-tree
`git add` pulling a concurrent agent's half-finished file into the wrong commit; `git mv`/`git rm`
staging themselves so another worktree's move lands in your commit no matter how careful your `git add`
is; and two scripts that mutate the owner's world, one of which overwrites the dated verification report
inside the archive bundle. A rule in a markdown file is enforced by whether the agent read that far.
tasks.evidence: Proven in both directions, which is the only way a gate is worth anything. THE GATE: a failing check reports FAIL and exits 1; `done` then refuses it; `done` refuses a task never verified at all; and appending an entry to `verify` AFTER verifying is refused by name — the cheapest laundering route, closed. THE GUARD: 13 command shapes, 6 blocked (`-A`, `--all`, bare `.`, one buried mid-chain, and both mutating scripts) and 7 allowed (explicit path lists, `git add -p`, a grep that merely MENTIONS a forbidden script, and the GUARD_OK=1 escape); staged `D` and `R100` each blocked in a scratch repo, with a clean index passing. MEASURED: 207 of 259 entries runnable, and every prose entry on an open task is on an owner task, so the runner covers the entire remaining agent queue. `workplan check` ok at 136 tasks.

notes: 2026-07-28 A HOOK MUST EXIT 2 TO BLOCK. Exit 1 is treated as a non-fatal hook error and the command runs anyway, so a guard written with `exit 1` reads exactly like a working guard and stops nothing — the same shape as a test that only passes. Two of this task's verify entries assert the number 2 specifically rather than merely non-zero, because that is the assertion that would catch the regression.

The hook does the real pattern work; the deny entries earn their place by making the intent visible in a file people actually read. Do not add a rule to `deny` and consider it enforced.

They are historical record, nothing will run them again, and prefixing them would be 25 edits to closed work for no behaviour change. Every prose entry on an OPEN task is prefixed, which is the set that matters. tasks.why:
Anthropic's published guidance, checked against what this project has actually paid for:

SEPARATE FRESH-CONTEXT VERIFIERS OUTPERFORM SELF-CRITIQUE. This is the finding with the most weight here,
because QUA-47, QUA-45 and the bundle guard each shipped a test suite that could not fail, and each passed
every check that existed. `my test passes and looks plausible` is not self-detecting. So the verifier gets
NO WRITE TOOLS: a verifier that can edit the thing it is judging stops being one the first moment editing
is easier than reporting.

A SINGLE VERIFICATION CALL BEAT A PANEL in Anthropic's measurements — multiple judges were WORSE, not
better. That inverted my own plan, which had a reviewer panel in it. One agent, run once.

CODING IS NAMED THE WORST FIT FOR PARALLEL MULTI-AGENT WORK: subagents cannot share the running context
that keeps edits consistent. Fan out to READ, never to write. `claim`'s file lock already encodes this.

AND THE TOOL OBSOLETED AN AGENT. A cheap Haiku `measurer` was planned alongside this to run verify lists.
QUA-53 does that deterministically for almost nothing, so the agent was dropped rather than shipped as
redundant surface. Worth noticing when a script removes the need for a model instead of the reverse.

tasks.title: Universal Links are dead in production — the Pages artifact carries no dot-path at all
tasks.done_when: https://akashic.no/.well-known/apple-app-site-association returns 200 with an applinks document, and the deploy asserts it after every push so it cannot silently regress.
tasks.why:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 against production: that URL returned 404 and served the SPA shell, so iOS could
not associate the domain and EVERY Universal Link was dead. Discriminating measurement from the same
build: /CNAME and /offline.html answered 200 while /.DS_Store and /.well-known/... both answered 404.
GitHub Pages was filtering every path beginning with a dot, and `.nojekyll` was absent.

THE INSTRUCTIVE PART IS WHY EVERYTHING WAS GREEN. `public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` is
committed, Vite copies it into `dist/`, and SHIP-07 closed on a verify list that grepped the
entitlements file — it never fetched the URL iOS actually reads. So the file was present in the
artefact and absent from the site, which no build-side check can see. Same family as the
INFOPLIST_KEY_* trap and the tokenless-bundle trap: the thing that is missing is invisible unless
something asserts on the SERVED artefact.

It was also caught by accident. LEG-09 carried the entry `curl -s <that URL> | head -5`, written
precisely to check this, whose exit status was `head`'s and so could never fail. Making the ledger
entries capable of failing is what surfaced it — the defect and the reason it hid are the same defect.
verify: MANUAL: read the Deploy to GitHub Pages run for the commit that lands this — the step "Assert the served site serves an applinks document" must be green. It cannot run until a push to main happens.
notes: 2026-07-28 THE FIRST FIX WAS WRONG, AND THE ASSERTION IS WHAT CAUGHT IT — which is the whole argument for asserting on the served artefact rather than the build. I added `public/.nojekyll` on the theory that Pages filters dot-paths through Jekyll, pushed, and the new post-deploy step went RED anyway: both the AASA and `.nojekyll` itself answered 404. The artifact tar listing settled it — `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4` tarred 55 files out of `dist/` and NOT ONE dot-path. So the exclusion happens at UPLOAD, not at serving, and no serving-side setting could ever have fixed it. Jekyll was never involved. Had I shipped the `.nojekyll` theory with a build-side check only, it would have looked fixed and stayed broken.

2026-07-28 THE FIX IS THE ROOT LOCATION. `public/apple-app-site-association` has no leading dot, so it reaches the artifact; Apple tries `/.well-known/` first and falls back to the root, so the root alone is sufficient. The `.well-known` copy and `.nojekyll` are kept because they cost nothing and become correct if the upload action ever carries dotfiles — but they are NOT what makes this work, and a future reader should not delete the root copy on the assumption that `.well-known` covers it.

2026-07-28 UNVERIFIED AND IT NEEDS A DEVICE: GitHub Pages serves an extensionless file as `application/octet-stream`, and Apple historically wanted `application/json`. iOS fetches the document through Apple's own CDN, which is more lenient, so this may be fine — but the only place it becomes a fact is SHIP-15, tapping a real link on a real device. If Universal Links still fail with the document served and valid, Content-Type is the next thing to check, and Pages cannot set it — that would mean moving the document to a host that can.

2026-07-28 HOW IT HID FOR SO LONG: SHIP-07 closed on a verify list that grepped the entitlements file and never fetched the URL iOS reads, and LEG-09 carried `curl -s <that URL> | head -5` — written to catch exactly this, and incapable of failing because its exit status was `head`'s. Making the ledger's entries capable of failing is what surfaced it. `public/.DS_Store` was tracked too, and was untracked in the same commit.

tasks.title: On cellular, a fresh install shows "Start your first journey" while the whole archive waits silently
tasks.done_when: A fresh install on a metered connection shows the family's journeys as named, visibly un-downloaded rows with an honest size and a "Download now" action — instead of the first-run hero — and the first-sync estimate matches what the engine actually fetches.
tasks.why:
MEASURED 2026-07-28, owner-reported ("enten laste ned alt eller ikke se noenting"). Three findings:

1. THE DEFERRED STATE IS INVISIBLE WHERE IT MATTERS. NetworkPolicy defaults to Wi-Fi-only downloads
(the right protective default), and on an expensive path AkashicSyncEngine defers the ENTIRE first
fetch and sets status .waitingForWiFi. That status surfaces in exactly one place: a row in Settings
(SettingsView.swift:115). JourneyListView renders store.journeys.isEmpty as JourneyEmptyState — the
"Start your first journey" onboarding hero. So a family member installing on cellular sees an empty
app inviting them to CREATE their first journey while the family archive exists and waits. Actively
misleading, not merely quiet — and it is precisely the state a beta household on holiday installs in.

2. THE ALL-OR-NOTHING IS THE GATE'S SCOPE, NOT THE ARCHITECTURE'S. The v2 media split already does
the hard half: media zones (originals, GBs) are excluded from every engine fetch
(mediaZoneIDsToExclude) and originals stream on demand — MediaFetcher explicitly allows a tapped
photo on cellular by design. What the Wi-Fi gate defers is journey zones: metadata + thumbnails.
The metadata alone (names, dates, days, routes, captions) is KBs and would render most of the app.

3. THE HONEST NUMBER IS STALE BY ~40x. SyncSizeEstimate.averagePhotoBytes is 3.5 MB, documented as
"originals + thumbnail" — but post-v2 the engine never fetches originals on first sync, so the
prompt would present a multi-GB figure for a ~75-97 MB thumbnail pull. A protective dialog that
overstates by 40x teaches people to decline it.

MINIMAL DESIGN (the owner asked for smarter WITHOUT overcomplicating):
(a) A lightweight, ungated, no-asset pre-fetch of journey summaries — a CKQueryOperation with
desiredKeys (name, dates, photo count), same pattern as the existing RemotePhotoCounting seam —
shown as real rows in JourneyListView in an un-downloaded state with "Waiting for Wi-Fi" and the
corrected size.
(b) One "Download now" action on that surface, wired to the release mechanism that already exists
(onAllowsHeavyTransferBecameTrue fires the deferred fetch); prefer a one-time override to flipping
the persistent setting.
(c) Fix the estimate to thumbnail scale for what first sync actually pulls, and say that full-quality
photos load when viewed.
EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, noted as the future option it is: per-journey selective download. The
zone-per-journey design makes it expressible later via fetch scope, but it is exactly the
overcomplication to avoid in the first cut.

tasks.title: DIFF-15 on a real device: the prompt worked, the rows did not — and the failure is undiagnosable by design
tasks.done_when: The un-downloaded journeys surface renders on a real device against Production (or its failure is visible and diagnosable from the device), sync/download progress is visible in the journey list, and a TestFlight build can produce a sync log the owner can read.
tasks.why:
MEASURED BY THE OWNER on build 101, fresh TestFlight install on cellular, the exact scenario DIFF-15
was built for: the first-sync size prompt APPEARED ("fikk beskjed om å vente på WiFi") — so
RemotePhotoCounting reached Production and returned a count — but the journey list showed NO
un-downloaded rows. The one path no simulator could exercise is the one that failed.

AND THE FAILURE CANNOT BE DIAGNOSED FROM THE DEVICE, WHICH IS THE FIRST DEFECT: the summarizer logs
its errors and its success count through SyncLog, and SyncLog is enabled ONLY by the AKASHIC_SYNC_LOG
environment variable — which a TestFlight install cannot set. The one surface where DIFF-15 can fail
(signed build, real CloudKit) is the one surface with no way to see why. DIFF-15's ledger note
called silent-nil "quiet and safe"; measured on device, silent means UNDIAGNOSABLE.

HYPOTHESES, ordered by what the evidence supports — the count query working narrows it usefully:
(a) UI/ordering: summaries publish after the list rendered, or the prompt interaction flips the
deferral state the row-branch requires (the third condition hides rows when no deferral is active);
(b) the per-zone Journey CKQuery fails against the DEPLOYED Production schema even though
schema.ckdb declares ___recordID QUERYABLE — deployed-vs-declared drift, checkable with a cktool
schema export (owner credentials, SHIP-15 territory);
(c) the summarizer runs exactly once at activation with no retry, so any transient failure is a
permanent hero until relaunch.

THE FIX SET: (1) a persisted dev-tools toggle for SyncLog (UserDefaults, not env) so a TestFlight
build can log and the owner can read it in Console.app — diagnosis before cleverness; (2) the
row-branch distinguishes "no remote journeys" from "could not check" while a deferral is active,
so a query failure stops impersonating a brand-new family; (3) retry the summary on path change /
foreground, same trigger family as onAllowsHeavyTransferBecameTrue; (4) THE OWNER'S SECOND POINT,
which stands on its own: sync happens invisibly in the background — when a download is actually
running, the list should show it (per-journey progress or an indeterminate state), because "things
appear eventually" reads as broken even when it is working.
